authored_seams.name: FA_FIXTURE
authored_seams.scope: All runtime configurations expose fa_fixture_begin, fa_fixture_step and fa_fixture_inspect; the no-seam fa_run configuration is compile-only.

authored_seams.name: fa_fixture_begin captured_state
authored_seams.scope: Caller pre-observation supplied as a value. Baseline CAS ignores it as authorization; admit-second control consumes stale Virgin after CAS refusal. Both control schedules stop before second selection.

authored_seams.name: serial event stepping
authored_seams.scope: READY_ENTER, ENTERED, RAW_AVAILABLE and RECORDED plus READY_COMPLETE publication cut. Withholding a step leaves Active; no process fault, signal, cancellation or nonlocal exit is executed.

authored_seams.name: private diagnostics
authored_seams.scope: Winning driver is stopped while inspect copies working/raw state. No concurrent public progress API; only state or acquired immutable result is public.

authored_seams.name: provider scripts
authored_seams.scope: Fixed process-image mutable scripts remain alive through execution. Raw script values are authored and do not measure native errno, file outcomes, addresses, frames or actual ownership.

build_contract.control_execution: Eight dedicated fresh-process exact-singleton controls per mode; no crashes, timeouts or sanitizer diagnostics accepted.
build_contract.retention: Before any build capture exact source lock, plan/reference sources and contract; immutable phase results, complete command specs/receipts/streams, ELF/disassembly and all raw reports. Failed packet terminal, no successful command/matrix replay.
build_contract.standalone: Two no-FA_FIXTURE objects compile-only; runtime uses authored scheduling seam.

admit-second-contender.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
admit-second-contender.mutation: A and B preobserve Virgin; omit the single combined CAS-winner veto for B and admit using its cached observation; stop before selection.

derive-owner-from-write-success.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
derive-owner-from-write-success.mutation: On ordinary write failure, clear the selected Community result instead of retaining it; other outcome fields remain exact.

invent-unreturned-write-result.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
invent-unreturned-write-result.mutation: At held write entry synthesize success in the authoritative winner-private working receipt: set return-recorded/raw-result fields that would feed completion. Inspect serially without later operations or public completion.

omit-owner-id-copy.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
omit-owner-id-copy.mutation: Keep the safe caller-owned value reference instead of copying ID bytes; change the still-live canonical source array to a different valid same-length 32-byte ID before finalization, without changing bounds or validity.

reopen-after-unknown.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
reopen-after-unknown.mutation: At held write entry, let a second request treat Active as Virgin; observe its admission and stop before its selection.

retain-stale-errno-after-success.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
retain-stale-errno-after-success.mutation: On successful fd=0 copy the authored stale errno sentinel and mark it failure-valid rather than retaining valid=false.

retry-short-write.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
retry-short-write.mutation: On positive short return author one extra modeled write event before the unchanged fsync/close sequence; no native I/O.

skip-close-after-write-error.isolation: Dedicated fresh value-only selector asserts this semantic boundary once; other checks are infrastructure only. No duplicate downstream veto may mask the mutation.
skip-close-after-write-error.mutation: After returned write=-1, skip the paired fsync/close continuation while retaining the owner and raw write result.

limits: Sequential value schedules are not concurrent C executions, signal/reentry tests or nonlocal exits.
Normal retained object/disassembly does not prove lock-free signal safety, transitive libc/canary/interposition behavior or weak-memory/native visibility.
No actual attribution, loader, DSO, installer, generated transfer, target/replacement invocation, native frame or crash-file provider.
NoCommunity says nothing about live-mod/time/append/quarantine internals. Returned IO classifications do not establish persisted blame, causal fault ownership or recovery.
No implementation change to frozen consumer, handlers, official core, protection, quarantine, package, emulator or physical deck; all live gates CLOSED.
prebuild_review_corrections: Admission-ba now reverses actual script custody and expected owner, not only actor labels; report retains both scripts.
Core helper noinline/noclone attributes align stable ELF function-extent observation with GCC; no atomic/lock-free or call-free oracle is claimed.
Runner schema aligns complete private serial snapshots and explicit source-scope facts; process/container cleanup survives interrupted-prefix capture failure.
scope: Separately authored offline C11 value-only terminal fault-attempt admission; no frozen consumer invocation or integration.
source_relationship: core.c/core.h/test_fault.c are new authored sources. No SDK/previous fixture function body is transformed, included, linked or executed. run-tests.py adapts prior command capture, immutable receipt and bounded ELF metadata patterns; retained predecessor runner is reference only. The plan/readme and eleven source inputs are retained without old collector/matrix execution.

transformation_groups.implementation: Separate fa_* module with fixed zero-initialized process-image state, winner-private working value and immutable final value. Existing consumer/readers/receipt cut remain byte-unchanged.

Single strong acq_rel/acquire Virgin-to-Active CAS authority before script access. Losers return without touching winner payload/providers; cached observations do not authorize. Serial A/B and pre-CAS/nested schedules use live authored values; no actual race or thread.

Authored resolved Community index/process identity/canonical zero-padded 33-byte ID or NoCommunity. Nonempty 1..32-byte IDs are bounded value fixtures, not SDK ID approval. Baseline copies values; controlled omission borrows a still-live same-length array.

Six fixed event slots; selection plus open/write/fsync/close or opaque unblamed. Each event separately enters, receives an authored raw value, records a private receipt, then advances. No frame/module/DSO traversal or native fault I/O. Open zero valid, open failure terminates branch, every ordinary write continues through fsync/close.

Winner copies full final result then release-stores OrdinaryReturned. fa_observe zeroes output and acquire-loads state once; only OrdinaryReturned copies final payload. Stopped schedules expose working data only through explicit serial test seam. Raw oracle remains distinct from authoritative receipt.

Opaque NoCommunity event and exact eight FA_CONTROL_* mutations isolated to dedicated selectors. One control macro at a time under FA_FIXTURE. No retry/reset/reopen in baseline; six slots also bound extra-write control. Harness stdio writes only private evidence reports, not modeled crash persistence.
